subject.title: [Feature]: Cron should distinguish execution success from delivery failure and show warning instead of error

question: Should successful cron execution with failed post-run delivery become a first-class cron `warning` status, or should cron keep `status=ok` and surface the failure through `deliveryStatus` and `lastDeliveryError`?
rationale: Both shapes are technically plausible, but they create different API, UI, backoff, and external-consumer semantics that automation should not choose silently.

options.title: Use ok plus delivery fields
options.body: Keep `CronRunStatus` as execution-only and let Control UI render a warning from `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`; this matches the existing two-field model and the narrower proof-positive PR.

options.title: Add first-class warning status
options.body: Expand cron status to include `warning` across storage, Gateway schema, CLI/UI filters, plugin/API consumers, docs, and compatibility proof.

options.title: Keep delivery failure as error
options.body: Reject the split and continue treating required delivery failure as a cron error/backoff signal even when execution produced output.

recommendation.title: Use ok plus delivery fields
recommendation.body: Keep `CronRunStatus` as execution-only and let Control UI render a warning from `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`; this matches the existing two-field model and the narrower proof-positive PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest recent history across the isolated cron delivery and session-target surfaces involved in the product contract choice.
